'''Xplore Inc.''' is a Canadian [[rural internet|rural]] [[internet service provider]]. It is the largest rural focused broadband service provider in Canada.

==History==
Xplore Inc. was founded in 2004 under the name Barrett XPlore.<ref>{{cite web|title=Company Overview of Xplornet Communications Inc.|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/private/snapshot.asp?privcapId=4612085|website=Bloombery|access-date=29 June 2015}}</ref>

In 2011, Barrett XPlore rebranded to Xplornet Communications Inc.<ref>{{Cite web |last=O'Brien |first=Greg |date=2011-05-26 |title=Barrett Xplore becomes Xplornet Communications |url=https://cartt.ca/barrett-xplore-becomes-xplornet-communications/ |access-date=2022-12-13 |website=Cartt.ca |language=en-CA}}</ref>

In April 2012, Xplore entered into a partnership with [[Shaw Communications]] to market bundles of its [[Shaw Direct]] satellite television service with Xplore internet service.<ref name="gandm-xplornetshaw">{{cite news|title=Shaw, Xplornet team up to bundle rural delivery|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/globe-investor/shaw-xplornet-team-up-to-bundle-rural-delivery/article4098833/|website=The Globe and Mail|date=4 April 2012 |access-date=28 May 2016|last1=Trichur |first1=Rita }}</ref>

In 2014, the company purchased capacity on [[ViaSat-2]] and EchoStar XIX as part of a plan to expand its service area to all of Canada by 2017.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Henry|first1=Caleb|title=Xplornet Charts Path to 100 Mbps Broadband Speed Using HTS|url=http://www.satellitetoday.com/telecom/2014/10/02/xplornet-charts-path-to-100-mbps-broadband-speed-using-hts/|access-date=29 June 2015|work=Satellite Today|date=October 2, 2014}}</ref><ref name=cbc>{{cite news|title=Xplornet pledges fast internet for rural, remote areas|url=http://www.cbc.ca/news/business/xplornet-pledges-fast-internet-for-rural-remote-areas-1.2720297|access-date=29 June 2015|work=CBC News|date=July 28, 2014}}</ref>

In January 2017, Xplore acquired the Saskatoon-based competitor YourLink.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rural internet provider YourLink to come under new ownership|url=https://thestarphoenix.com/business/local-business/rural-internet-provider-yourlink-to-come-under-new-ownership|website=Saskatoon Star-Phoenix|access-date=19 June 2017}}</ref>

In November 2017, Xplore acquired Manitoba-based fixed wireless provider [[Netset Communications]]. With the deal Xplore retained the Netset brand and Netset continues to operate out of [[Brandon, Manitoba]] as a separate division of Xplore.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.xplornet.com/about/news/xplornet-communications-inc-announces-major-investment-manitoba/|title=Xplornet Communications Inc. Announces Major Investment in Manitoba - Xplornet|work=Xplornet|access-date=2018-08-14|language=en-US|archive-date=2020-09-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200918113700/https://www.xplornet.com/about/news/xplornet-communications-inc-announces-major-investment-manitoba/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

During the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], Xplore customers reported increased issues with connectivity speeds. According to Lis McWalter, a Carling, Ontario resident and chair of the West Parry Sound SMART Community Network, speeds are so slow that audio calls are impeded, and said "Even at the best of times we don't get the speed that's promised."<ref>{{Cite news |date=2020-03-26 |title=Rural Internet Users Frustrated by Slow Speeds |language=en-US |work=The Sun |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200327125221/https://www.thestar.com/business/2020/03/26/rural-internet-users-frustrated-by-slow-connections-as-providers-struggle-with-data-overages.html |url-status=live |url=https://www.thestar.com/business/rural-internet-users-frustrated-by-slow-connections-as-providers-struggle-with-data-overages/article_457f508f-ffc0-5798-8a69-d7d6e720ada4.html |archive-date=2020-03-27 |url-access=subscription |access-date=2020-03-26}}</ref>

In June 2020, Xplore announced its sale to New York private equity firm [[Stonepeak Infrastructure Partners]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.xplore.ca/about/news/xplornet-announces-completion-of-sale-to-stonepeak-infrastructure-partners/|title=Xplornet Announces Completion of Sale to Stonepeak Infrastructure Partners|date=2022-06-11|access-date=2022-09-16|work=Press release}}</ref> The sale did not include Xplore Mobile, which continued as a separate company before shutting down at the end of August 2022.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Karadeglija |first=Anja |date=2022-07-19 |title=Xplore Mobile shut down is a signal for government to 'stop approving telecom mergers' |language=en |work=National Post |url=https://nationalpost.com/news/politics/xplore-mobile-shut-down-signal-for-government-to-stop-approving-telecom-mergers |access-date=2022-08-15}}</ref>

In September 2022, rebranded from Xplornet Communications Inc. to ''Xplore Inc.''<ref>{{cite web |url=https://mobilesyrup.com/2022/09/13/xplornet-undergoes-rebranding-is-now-known-as-xplore/|title=Xplornet undergoes rebranding, is now known as Xplore|last=Zafar|first=Nida|date=2022-09-13|access-date=2022-09-16}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.newswire.ca/news-releases/xplornet-rebrands-to-xplore-800914685.html|title=Xplornet Rebrands to Xplore|date=2022-09-13|access-date=2022-09-16|work=Press release}}</ref>

==Services==
Xplore provides fixed wireless internet access to remote areas through a combination of fibre, [[satellite internet]] as well as [[LTE (telecommunication)|LTE]] and [[WiMAX]]  [[fixed wireless]] networks. It owns part of the lifetime capacity of [[ViaSat-2]] and is expanding its 4G and 5G network. These networks support approximately 400,000 subscribers, the largest number of rural Canadian subscribers of any company as of 2021.<ref name=cbc />

As with other telecommunications companies, some Xplore programs are funded in part by federal and provincial government grants.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.xplornet.com/about/government-programs/|title=Government programs|work=Xplornet.com|access-date=September 30, 2020|archive-date=September 29, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200929065956/https://www.xplornet.com/about/government-programs/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In September 2021, Xplore announced that it was launching Canada's first rural 5G standalone network starting in New Brunswick.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Xplornet Launching Canada’s First Rural 5G Standalone Network |url=https://www.xplore.ca/about/news/xplornet-launching-canadas-first-rural-5g-standalone-network/ |access-date=2022-12-13 |website=Xplore |language=en-CA}}</ref>

Xplore is rolling out a fibre-to-the-premise network offering speeds up to one gigabit per second in seven provinces with more projects to come. The company is investing $500 million by 2025 to deploy state-of-the-art scalable fibre Internet and fibre-powered 5G fixed wireless technology in its facilities-based network. Xplore currently has fibre projects underway in Alberta, Manitoba, Ontario, Quebec, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia and Prince Edward Island.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Xplore Fibre Launching in Quebec |url=https://www.xplore.ca/about/news/xplore-fibre-launching-in-quebec/ |access-date=2022-12-13 |website=Xplore |language=en-CA}}</ref>

In November 2022, Xplore announced that residents and businesses in rural and remote regions will have access to download speeds up to 100 megabits per second (Mbps) and more data on the company's next-generation satellite service, starting in the summer of 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Xplore Fibre Launching in Quebec |url=https://www.xplore.ca/about/news/xplore-fibre-launching-in-quebec/ |access-date=2022-12-13 |website=Xplore |language=en-CA}}</ref>

=== Xplore Mobile ===
On February 16, 2017, Bell announced that as part of its acquisition of [[Manitoba Telecom Services]] (MTS), it would divest a portion of its wireless subscribers to Xplornet. The divestment was a condition of the deal intended to preserve the presence of four major wireless carriers in Manitoba post-merger (Bell also divested a larger portion of MTS's wireless subscribers to [[Telus Communications|Telus]]). Xplornet would receive 24,700 MTS subscribers, as well as 6 retail locations, and wireless spectrum. Bell entered into agreements with Xplornet to provide tower access, roaming, and devices for a period of time while it establishes its new mobile network.<ref name="gandm-xplornetbell">{{cite news|title=Ottawa approves BCE-MTS tie-up; deal to benefit Xplornet|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/report-on-business/bce-mts-deal-wins-federal-approval/article34026683/|website=The Globe and Mail|date=15 February 2017 |access-date=15 February 2017|last1=Dobby |first1=Christine }}</ref><ref name="cbcnews-approved">{{cite web|title=Bell takeover of MTS gets federal approval|url=http://www.cbc.ca/news/business/bell-mts-approval-competition-1.3983774|website=CBC News|access-date=15 February 2017}}</ref>

The new Xplore Mobile brand was announced August 1, 2018. The company claimed that its wireless services would be "built on the values of fairness, simplicity and transparency".<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://mobilesyrup.com/2018/08/01/xplornet-announces-xplore-mobile-manitoba/|title=Xplornet announces new 'Xplore Mobile' wireless brand in Manitoba|date=2018-08-01|work=MobileSyrup|access-date=2018-08-01|language=en-US}}</ref> 

In July 2022, Xplornet announced that Xplore Mobile would end operations at the end of August 2022, citing it that had been impacted by "high roaming rates that significantly exceed retail prices", and regulatory delays in a new CRTC framework that would require the incumbent wireless carriers to sell wholesale access to their networks to new regional competitors for a period of time. Xplore Mobile's pricing was never competitive with that of Bell, Rogers, or Telus. Executive director of the Public Interest Advocacy Centre John Lawford argued that the divestment was not aggressive enough to make Xplore Mobile a viable competitor to the established incumbents, and that the company's failure demonstrated the federal government's lax attitude towards competition in Canada's wireless industry.<ref name=":0" />
